maths_errors.text: Forgetting the 'outside' region — placing all items inside the circles and getting a total that's too high.
maths_errors.correction: If you forget the outside region, the numbers in the diagram add up to too little, not too much. In the worked example the circles hold 11 + 7 + 7 = 25, which is 5 short of 30. The real mistake is that the diagram's total is too low, so the 'neither' count is missing. Alternatively, a student forces the circle values up to make them reach the grand total, which makes them wrong. Either way the stated consequence 'a total that's too high' is incorrect.

missing_spec_content.spec_text: enumerate sets and combinations of sets systematically, using tables, grids, Venn diagrams
missing_spec_content.why: Only Venn diagrams are taught. Systematic listing of outcomes, sample-space tables and grids are not covered. Enumerating the actual elements of sets (for example listing which numbers belong in A, B, A ∩ B, A ∪ B and A') is not taught. The universal set symbol ξ, used on exam Venn diagrams, is never introduced; the lesson only calls it 'the rectangle'.

missing_spec_content.spec_text: Additional foundation: including using tree diagrams
missing_spec_content.why: Tree diagrams are not mentioned anywhere in the lesson.

missing_spec_content.spec_text: calculate and interpret conditional probabilities through representation using expected frequencies with two-way tables, tree diagrams and Venn diagrams
missing_spec_content.why: Conditional probability is not taught at all. There is no P(A | B) idea, no 'given that' questions and no restricting the denominator to one circle. Two-way tables, tree diagrams and expected frequencies are also missing.

above_gcse.why: The n(…) notation for 'number of elements' is not used in AQA GCSE papers and is never defined in the lesson. A student meeting it for the first time may think n is a variable to be multiplied. Writing 'number in A ∩ B ÷ total' says the same thing in plain words.

cases_not_modelled.case: Listing the elements of sets (for example ξ = {1,…,12}, A = multiples of 3, B = even numbers) and placing them in a Venn diagram
cases_not_modelled.why: The only worked example uses frequencies. Placing actual elements into regions is the core of 'enumerate sets' and is never shown.

cases_not_modelled.case: Finding P(A ∪ B) from a Venn diagram
cases_not_modelled.why: Union is defined and the addition formula is given, but no worked example calculates a union probability.

cases_not_modelled.case: Finding P(A ∩ B) from a Venn diagram
cases_not_modelled.why: The example finds P(French only), not the probability of the intersection.

cases_not_modelled.case: Finding a complement probability P(A') from a Venn diagram
cases_not_modelled.why: The key facts warn that A' includes the B-only region, but no example counts A' or uses 1 − P(A).

cases_not_modelled.case: Venn diagram where an unknown region must be found algebraically (for example the intersection is x)
cases_not_modelled.why: This is a common question type and is not modelled.

cases_not_modelled.case: Venn diagram filled with probabilities rather than frequencies
cases_not_modelled.why: All examples use counts. Working with decimal or fraction probabilities that sum to 1 is not shown.

cases_not_modelled.case: Sample-space table or grid for two events
cases_not_modelled.why: Tables and grids are named in the specification but no example uses one.
Additional foundation content with no example.

cases_not_modelled.case: Conditional probability from a Venn diagram (for example P(French | German) = 7/14)
cases_not_modelled.why: No example restricts the denominator to one set.

cases_not_modelled.case: Conditional probability from a two-way table or tree diagram using expected frequencies

density.text: the left-only region contains items in set A but not B; the right-only region contains items in B but not A; the overlapping (intersection) region contains items in both A and B; and the outside region (inside the rectangle but outside both circles) contains items in neither set.
density.why: A single sentence defines four regions and introduces the term 'intersection', with nothing drawn to look at. This is hard to hold in mind in one read.

density.text: A ∩ B (intersection) = items in both A and B  |  A ∪ B (union) = items in A or B or both  |  A' (complement) = items not in A  |  P(A ∩ B) = n(A ∩ B) ÷ total  |  P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B)  |  P(A') = 1 − P(A)
density.why: Three new symbols and three probability formulas are packed into one line separated by bars, with no example of any of them.

density.text: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B) avoids double-counting the intersection.
density.why: The reason is asserted rather than shown. It does not explain that the overlap is included in both P(A) and P(B), so adding them counts it twice.

density.text: Fill the Venn diagram. The intersection (both) = 7. French only = 18 − 7 = 11. German only = 14 − 7 = 7.
density.why: Three placements and two subtractions are in one step. The reason for subtracting 7 (the 18 French students already include the 7 who do both) is not stated.

density.text: Writing the total for a circle (e.g. 18) in the intersection region instead of only the 'both' count (7), then double-counting items.
density.why: This describes putting 18 in the intersection, but the correction is about putting 11 in the French-only region. The usual error is writing 18 in the A-only region. The mismatch makes the mistake hard to picture.

not_checked: No Venn diagram image is included or described visually. Whether a diagram is rendered alongside the worked example, and whether it matches 11, 7, 7 and 5, could not be checked.
